listings.name: Hangang Citizen's Park
listings.content: Alongside the Han River through 13 districts: Gwangnaru, Jamsil, Gangdong, Ttukseom, Jamwon, Banpo, Ichon, Yeouido, Yanghwa, Mangwon, Seonyudo, Nanji, and Gangseojigu. You can see many people strolling or jogging along the trail paths, as well as in-line skaters, bicyclists, and soccer fields or basketball courts. Yeouido, Jamsil, and Ttukseom districts are especially popular because of the cruise services on the Han River.

listings.name: Gwanghwamun Plaza
listings.content: A center of Seoul. The name came from the main gate of the Gyeongbokgung. The site was a location of the Six Ministries during the Joseon dynasty and was a large motorway since then. In 2009, the middle of the road was opened to the public as a renovation project. It's now home to festivals and events. There are two statues in the plaza: Admiral Yi Sun-sin (a legendary admiral who won numerous important battles against Japanese invaders) and Sejong the Great (the most famous and popular king in Korean history, inventor of the Korean alphabet). The original gate was demolished by the Japanese during the colonial period, but has been faithfully rebuilt in its original location. Today, visitors can watch the changing of the guard ceremony performed by soldiers of the South Korean military dressed in Joseon-era historical costumes at 10:00 and 14:00 every day except Tuesdays.

listings.name: Gyeongbokgung
listings.content: This is Seoul's grandest Joseon Dynasty-era palace and the seat of power for centuries before it was razed in 1592 by a Japanese invasion (and again by the Japanese in 1910). This was the first palace used by the Joseon Dynasty and was constructed after King Taejo founded the Joseon Dynasty and moved the capital to Hanyang. Large parts have now been restored, and the vast grounds also house the Joseon Palace Museum and the Korean Folk Museum. There's a small corner where you get the chance to try on traditional Korean dress for free after registering. Changing of the royal guard at Gwanghwamun (광화문, 光化門), the elegantly restored main gate to the palace, occurs twice a day at 10:00 and 14:00, as soldiers from the South Korean army dressed in Joseon-era uniforms march with traditional weapons to the tune of drumbeats for 20 minutes.

listings.name: Changdeokgung
listings.content: Second only to Gyeongbokgung in historical importance, it was built in 1405 and was the seat of power between 1618 and 1896. The buildings have been restored to create a dazzling but still elegant effect that got the palace listed as a . The site is better preserved than Gyeongbokgung. Buildings of particular note include the blue-roofed Seonjeongjeon, which was the King's office, and the Daejojeon ("Great Making Hall"), his bedchamber, but perhaps most famous of all is the Huwon ("Secret Garden") in the back. Access to the garden is by guided tour only, except on Thursdays when only self-guided tours are available in summer from April to August. English tours are only offered at 10:30 and 14:30 and last around 60 minutes with a walking distance of about 2.5 km, including some steps and incline for the Huwon portion (the grounds are wheelchair-accessible for most parts but may have to enter certain areas in a reverse direction from the group). Trivia: The building structure is not symmetrical and has a more natural-oriented arrangement than the Gyeongbokgung. You may find some Western influences in some buildings which were introduced during the late 1800s, such as a chandelier and the elevated pathway for the automobile.

listings.name: Changgyeonggung
listings.content: It was built in 1104 as a summer palace for the Kings of the Goryeo Dynasty and became one of the main palaces during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace was used as a temporary home for the King during the time Gyeongbuk Palace was being built. Unlike other palaces that have a North-South orientation, Changgyeong Palace faces East-West. Also, this palace is known for connecting to Jongmyo Shrine, a holy place for the Joseon Dynasty, where sacrificial rites are practiced for previous kings and queens. Sadly, the buildings were largely demolished during the Japanese occupation (1910—1945). The name was changed to Changgyeongwon (literally Changgyeong park), and the site was used as a zoo. Restoration began during the 1980s, and the zoo was moved to Gwacheon, which is now Seoul Grand Park.

listings.name: Gyeonghui-gung
listings.content: It was built in the 17th century, and was burnt down twice in the 19th century. It was largely destroyed by the Japanese during colonial rule to build a school for Japanese children. It was finally restored in 1985 and opened to the public.

listings.name: Unhyeongung
listings.content: A museum in the former palace of a Joseon Dynasty archduke Heungseon, who was the father of the second last king of Joseon. It has several mannequins depicting the costumes of the yangban or noble class during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace buildings themselves represent the style of the Joseon noble class' mansion well.

listings.name: Jongmyo Shrine
listings.content: The royal ancestral temple during the Joseon Dynasty, this is where the kings would perform sacrificial rituals in honor of their ancestors. Certainly, the most famous shrine devoted to the royal family members of Korean dynasties. The grounds are a bit more walker-friendly than some of the palaces, admission is cheaper, and they also have some interactive equipment available to learn about the rituals and ceremonies used to treat deceased royal family members, but the interior of the shrine buildings is off-limits to the public. The Jongmyo Shrine is a . The Jongmyo Jerye (종묘제례) ceremony, which is still led by the head of the former royal family, is held here on the first Sunday of May every year, during which there will be traditional Korean performances as part of the ceremony, and the only time when the public can view (but not enter) the interior of the shrine buildings. English guided tours at 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00.

listings.name: Jogyesa Temple
listings.content: The chief temple of the Jogye order of Buddhism, the dominant branch of Buddhism in Korea. As such, it is one of the most important modern Buddhist temples in the country. That being said, Jogyesa Temple is rather small, and if time permits, Bongeunsa in Gangnam is a larger and more interesting Buddhist temple.

listings.name: Dongdaemun Gate
listings.content: More formally known as Heunginjimun (흥인지문, 興仁之門), the old eastern gate of the city still stands. Though not as impressive architecturally as Namdaemun, the Dongdaemun market is infinitely more interesting than its counterpart.

listings.name: Sukjeongmun Gate
listings.address: San 25-22, Samcheong-dong 서울 성북구 성북동 산 25-22

listings.name: National Folk Museum Children's Museum
listings.content: This place provides various experiences and services for children in areas such as exhibitions, education, research, and exchange.
listings.image: External View of the National Folk Museum of Korea, Seoul.jpg

listings.name: Hyehwa Moon
listings.content: It is located at the border between Seongbuk-gu and Jongno-gu, and it is related to Jongno-gu, so I inserted it in the Jongno-gu compartment.

listings.name: Museum Kimchikan
listings.content: A museum (previously known as Kimchi Field Museum) about all things kimchi. Includes a lot of interactive exhibits and comes with a free audio guide in English. There are also hands-on kimchi-making programs, only on reservation, however.

listings.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
listings.content: Since its independence from Japan, Korea has experienced a series of political events during a short period. You can see exhibitions that show war, dictatorships, uprisings against dictatorships, and industrialization that happened in South Korea.

listings.name: Seoul Museum of History
listings.content: Seoul has been the capital of Korea since 1392, and this museum focuses on its history during Joseon Dynasty, the Japanese annexation period, and modern development.

listings.name: Seoul Craft Museum
listings.content: The Seoul Craft Museum can experience the technical, practical, artistic, and cultural values of crafts by studying and sharing not only crafts but also knowledge, records, people, and the environment surrounding crafts.

listings.name: Seoul Museum of Education
listings.content: The Seoul Education Museum opened on June 15, 1995, by displaying relics and photographs on educational systems, curriculum, educational contents, educational institutions, and educational activities to establish the status of Seoul education and present a bright future for future generations in the 21st century.

listings.name: Beautiful Tea Museum
listings.content: You can see artifacts or pottery related to tea here.

listings.name: Police Museum
listings.content: The Police Museum, which opened in 2005, is a space where you can preserve the history of the police and experience the activities of the police.

listings.name: Hanyangdoseong Museum
listings.content: Hanyangdoseong Museum is a museum that contains the history and culture of Hanyangdoseong from the Joseon Dynasty to the present. It is a cultural space with a permanent exhibition room, special exhibition room, data room, and study room.

listings.name: Rice cake museum
listings.content: You can see relics related to rice cake.

listings.name: Seoul Our Sound Museum
listings.content: A unique museum where you can see and hear traditional culture.

listings.name: Newspaper Museum
listings.content: The Newspaper Museum offers a panoramic view of the 130-year history of Korean newspapers since the first modern newspaper in Korea, Hanseong Sunbo (1883).
listings.price: Adult ₩4000, elementary school students~ university students ₩3000, free for older than 65 years old

listings.name: National Weather Museum
listings.content: The National Weather Museum can see the development of modern weather technology from the history of weather observation to the current day world of supercomputers.

listings.name: Bukchon Oriental Culture Museum
listings.content: You can see various exhibitions of the museum, and there is an observatory where you can see Seoul City Wall and Gyeongbokgung Palace.

listings.name: World Museum of Decorations
listings.content: It is a space where you can learn the history, culture, society, and art of various ethnic groups through ornaments.

listings.name: National Museum of Buddhism
listings.content: This place works as a museum at the center of Korean Buddhism, it holds a meaningful special exhibition every year and can feel the traditional culture closer Prepare education.

listings.name: PKM gallery
listings.content: Established in 2001, PKM Gallery is known for its sleek, modern architecture and thoughtfully curated exhibitions that span painting, sculpture, multimedia, and installation art. The gallery actively participates in global art fairs and supports emerging and established artists alike, making it a significant player in South Korea's contemporary art scene. It offers visitors an immersive cultural experience, surrounded by beautiful views of the nearby Bukchon Hanok Village.

listings.name: Whanki Museum
listings.content: The Whanki Museum, nestled in the serene hills of Buam-dong in Seoul, is dedicated to the life and work of renowned Korean abstract artist Kim Whanki. Opened in 1992, this museum showcases Kim's distinctive abstract works that blend traditional Korean themes with modern abstract forms, creating a unique visual language. The museum’s architecture harmonizes with its natural surroundings, offering visitors a peaceful environment to appreciate art. In addition to its permanent collection, Whanki Museum also hosts special exhibitions and educational programs that explore various facets of contemporary Korean art. It’s a must-visit for those interested in Korean modern art and abstract expressionism.

listings.name: National Children's Science Museum
listings.content: It is a science museum for children.

listings.name: Tapgol ("Pagoda") Park
listings.content: A small park frequented by the elderly and the footsore traveler, just to the east of Jongmyo Shrine. Contains a 500-year-old namesake pagoda under protective glass and a nice large gazebo to get out of the sun. This is where the Korean constitution was first read aloud by the public during the 20th century. Acts as a navigation landmark when moving between Myeong-dong, Jong-no, and Insa-dong neighborhoods.

listings.name: Cheong Wa Dae
listings.content: Also known in English as the Blue House, it was the residence of the President of the Republic of Korea from 1948-2022. It's next to the grounds of Gyeongbokgung, and can be easily recognized by its blue roof tiles and its unique fusion of modern and traditional Korean architectural styles. It is now open to the public, but only allows a limited number of visitors per day, so be sure to reserve your tickets in advance. As of June 2025, president Lee Jae-myung have announced that he will soon move his presidential residence back to Cheong Wa Dae, so be quick if you wish to visit.

listings.name: Sungkyunkwan
listings.content: Sungkyunkwan was the highest educational institution during the Joseon dynasty since 1398. Students, including the royal family, studied Confucianism and other courses in Sungkyunkwan and became government officials and scholars. Munmyo was a Confucian shrine in Sungkyunkwan, and a ceremonial rite called 'Seokjeon Daeje' is performed twice a year. The current Sungkyunkwan University is a modern successor of Sungkyunkwan. Gingko trees in Autumn are very beautiful and famous.

listings.name: Cheonggyecheon
listings.content: It is a trail where you can take a walk along the river. The stream is a popular recreational area with walking paths, small waterfalls, and over 20 bridges, providing a peaceful escape in the heart of the city. Cheonggyecheon is also illuminated at night, making it a scenic spot for visitors to enjoy both the natural and urban landscapes. It’s especially popular during seasonal festivals, like the Seoul Lantern Festival, which takes place along its banks.

listings.name: Bukchon Observatory
listings.content: Provides a sweeping view of Bukchon Village and the greater Seoul cityscape, with Lotte Tower and the palace both clearly visible. It’s humble: clearly a converted apartment, and so tucked away its easy to miss, but it’s a great place to rest and take in the views, with beverage (tea, coffee) included as part of admission.

listings.name: Bukak palgakjung
listings.content: You can see the night view of Seoul from the observation deck located on Mt. Bukak.

listings.name: Hongik University Daehakro Art Center
listings.content: It is a musical theater and cultural complex consisting of a large theater with 702 seats, a small theater with 150 seats, and two large exhibition rooms. It has the best facilities in the nearby Daehak-ro area.
listings.address: 128-8 Hongik University Daehak-ro Art Center, Yeongeon-dong

listings.name: Naksan Park
listings.content: It is a park that runs from Dongdaemun to Hyehwa-dong. From the top of the park, you can see the night view of Seoul.

listings.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
listings.content: The collective name of the few tiny suburbs ("dong") wedged between Gyeongbuk Palace and the Secret Garden, just north of Insadong and Anguk Station. This area was where relatives of the royal family, high public officials, and other important families lived for over 500 years as they serviced the nearby palaces. Today, some 900 of their traditional Korean "hanok" houses remain, making this area one of Seoul's most picturesque centres for arts, culture, food, and fashion. The flip side is that the neighbourhood has been heavily commercialized, is rather soulless, and on the verge of becoming a Korean theme park. Some streets no longer house local residents and have instead been taken over entirely by guest houses in faux hanok style. From 17:00 to 10:00, tourists are not allowed to enter the village. Self-styled neighbourhood guards in fantasy uniforms patrol the streets and rudely shoo visitors away. If your accommodation is in the area, they will let you pass grudgingly, but take cruel pleasure in proclaiming an absurd photo ban during the curfew.

listings.name: Inwangsan Mountain
listings.content: This 336-m hill is home to the eponymous Inwang Temple (Inwangsa) and to Seoul's most famous shamanist shrine Guksadang (국사당). To get there, take Exit 2 and start climbing uphill following the "Inwang Temple" signs, through the huge construction site, and up through the temple gate. You'll see a map board and several paths. Take the left staircase upward, past the bronze bell of Bongwonsa, and you'll reach Guksadang. Behind it are several creeks with shamanist offerings and the bizarre rock formation known as the Zen Rocks; there are plenty of trails if you want to poke around, and the Seoul fortress wall can be seen running near the top of the hill. Be careful not to photograph or disturb any rituals you see being performed.

listings.name: Hyehwa
listings.content: Performing arts center. Many small theaters with live dramatic and comedic performances lining every street. This district is filled with life and street commerce past midnight. The name came after the Seoul National University, which was located here before it moved to Gwanak-gu. SNU Hospital and Seoul National University School of Medicine one of the best in the country, is still here.

listings.name: Sejong Center for Performing Arts
listings.content: Oldest and one of the largest multi-purpose theatres in downtown Seoul and home of Seoul Philharmonic. The biggest pipe organ in East Asia is in its Great Auditorium, and several video art pieces from Nam June Paik are in the entrance of the auditorium.

listings.name: Institute of Korean Royal Cuisine
listings.content: As the name implies, you learn how to prepare royal cuisine, as well as rice cakes and hangwa (Korean cookies).

listings.name: O'ngo Food Communications
listings.content: Learn to make authentic Korean dishes in English or Japanese from Korean chefs. O'ngo Food Communications offers classes to make bulgogi and kimchi, Korean barbecue, and Vegan Temple Cuisine. You get a tour of a traditional Korean Market after the classes to see Korean ingredients and people.

listings.name: The lantern light festival
listings.content: Every November, the lantern light festival takes place at Cheonggye Creek. At the festival, you can see many lanterns made by Korean and foreign artists. Some of the lanterns are in traditional Korean style, and there are also many character lanterns and company mascot lanterns.

listings.name: Rent Korean Traditional Clothes
listings.content: When you visit Gyeongbokgung (경복궁), Changdeokgung (창덕궁), or any palace near Jongno you can rent traditional Korean clothes and enter for a free visit. You will be able to embrace Korean culture and make great memories in Seoul. You can rent traditional Korean clothes for around ₩20,000, get a traditional Korean hairstyle for women and keep it for 2 hours.

listings.name: Aruto Small Theater
listings.content: Located in the Daehak-ro district, Aruto Small Theater is known for staging romantic comedies. Since 2023, the theater is showcasing the play "De-minus Back to Fall in Love," a lighthearted romantic comedy. This small venue offers a cozy setting for audiences to enjoy live theater in an informal atmosphere.

listings.name: LOL Park
listings.content: It is the place where League of Legends matches take place, and there are many PC rooms in the same building, so there are many things to enjoy

listings.name: Imun Seolnongtang
listings.content: The oldest extant restaurant in South Korea, founded around 1904. Serves seolleongtang (beef stew).

listings.name: Sadongmyenok
listings.content: Justly famous for its manduguk, a soup of gargantuan homemade dumplings stuffed with meat and veggies and served with side dishes for ₩5,000. English menu available.

listings.name: Gung
listings.content: Specialty restaurant for mandu (Korean dumplings) from the nearby Kaesong region in North Korea. The chickpea patties are also very good. This restaurant has been passed down from mother to daughter for three generations.

listings.name: Everest
listings.content: Nepali restaurant featuring dozens of delectable dishes ranging from mutton curry to butter naan. Bollywood music videos are free.

listings.name: Samcheong Sujaebi
listings.content: Canteen style ambiance, renowned for serving good Sujaebi - a mild soup where the noodles are flattened and torn into sheets. Always packed with people so be prepared for a queue.

listings.name: Tosokchon
listings.content: Reverently referenced in most local guides as the place for Ginseng chicken soup and variations on that theme.

listings.name: Hakrim Dabang
listings.content: Opened in 1956, this is the oldest extant coffee shop (in Korean, 다방; dabang) in Seoul. Known for its vintage charm, cozy wooden interiors, and retro vibe, Hakrim Dabang offers a nostalgic experience reminiscent of the old Seoul. It’s particularly famous for its hand-drip coffee, tea, and classic menu items like the "Vienna coffee," served with a generous topping of whipped cream. The café is a beloved spot for artists, writers, and students, providing a peaceful escape and a slice of Korean coffee culture in a timeless setting.

listings.name: Jung Don
listings.content: This restaurant serves Japanese-style pork cutlets. It's so popular that it's been featured on a popular Korean food program.

listings.name: Local Village(토속촌)
listings.content: It sells samgyetang, a traditional Korean dish, and ginseng liquor.

listings.name: Pitzeriao
listings.content: This is the place to go for wood-fired pizza. They serve pasta and pizza, so if you're looking for a western restaurant, this is the place to go.

listings.name: Yukhoe Sisterhood(육회자매집)
listings.content: In Korea, lean cuts of beef with less fat are cut into small pieces, seasoned, and eaten as sashimi. It tastes great when paired with the fruit pear and egg yolk. However, be careful when eating sashimi with octopus, also known 'San Naggi (산낙지)', as it can be offensive. Of course, the octopus is trimmed after it dies, but its nerves are still alive and it can wiggle.

listings.name: Manson Hoff
listings.content: It's known for its cold draft beer, nogari, and chicken. It's especially popular in the fall when the weather is nice and in the summer when it's hot.

listings.name: Tteoksang
listings.content: This restaurant offers a fusion of Korean tteokbokki (rice cakes) in a hanok charming setting.

listings.name: Pungnyeon Ssal Nongsan
listings.content: cheap snack places. noodle sausage, fried stuff, fried rice cake...

listings.name: Jin A Chun
listings.content: The second oldest operating restaurant in Seoul, having been founded in 1925. Serves Korean Chinese cuisine.

listings.name: Yukmian
listings.content: Yukmian is a restaurant that offers beef noodle dishes, located near Daehak-ro. The menu features various cuts of beef served with noodles in a broth. The restaurant is known for its focus on quality ingredients and simple preparation. Due to its popularity, reservations may be required during busy hours.

listings.name: a buckwheat-flavored restaurant
listings.content: This restaurant specializes in dishes made from buckwheat, offering a variety of traditional Korean meals. Located in the Daehak-ro area, it provides a menu that highlights buckwheat as a key ingredient, including noodles and pancakes. The simple setting and focus on buckwheat-based dishes attract those seeking a unique dining experience.

listings.name: UjauKimchi Tteokbokki
listings.content: Yuja Yoo Tteokbokki is a restaurant that specializes in tteokbokki, a popular Korean dish made from rice cakes. The restaurant offers a variety of tteokbokki options with different levels of spice and flavors.

listings.name: Hyehwa Dodam
listings.content: It is a famous restaurant for Korean traditional foods such as kimchi stew and pajeon. They also sell Korean traditional makgeolli.

listings.name: Hyehwa Gopchang
listings.content: It is a restaurant where you can eat assorted tripe at a low price.

listings.name: Uyeonhwa
listings.content: The Hanok-style restaurant in Ikseon-dong blends modern sensibilities and traditional atmosphere. It features Hamburg steak made with 100 percent Korean beef and is served with hot pot rice.

listings.name: Sinrajemyeon Anguk Branch
listings.content: It is a kalguksu specialty store that originated in Gyeongju, and is located in Anguk Station in Seoul. It features a traditional Korean interior with a luxurious atmosphere.

listings.name: Chwiyabeolguksi
listings.content: Dumpling hot pot is a particularly famous noodle restaurant. Dumpling hot pot here boasts a deep and cool taste of soup with a combination of large dumplings and fresh vegetables.

listings.name: Eomyongbaek pork soup
listings.content: It is a restaurant that serves Busan style pork and rice soup in a tranquil hanok atmosphere. The main menu here is pork and rice soup in two styles, clear and thick, and kimchi and kkakdugi, served as basic side dishes, go well with gukbap.

listings.name: GwanghwamunMijin
listings.content: As a traditional buckwheat specialty, cold buckwheat noodles and handmade pork cutlet are the main dishes. The restaurant is spacious and quick-rotating, and the Yeolmu Kimchi and pickled radish served as standard side dishes are delicious.

listings.name: Dooly snack
listings.content: It is a restaurant that sells snacks in Hyehwa-dong. It sells a variety of menus at low prices. You can only pay in cash.

listings.name: Queensgard
listings.content: The British pub. Introducing a range of lesser-known British drinks and foods, including infused gins, a variety of London dry gins, British beers, and ciders.

listings.name: CHILLIN
listings.content: An atmospheric cafe and bar on University Road.

listings.name: AcefourClub
listings.content: A coffee and liquor store in a converted tea room.

listings.name: Sunset Records
listings.content: It's a place that accepts submissions and enjoys singing and drinking.

listings.name: Friends
listings.content: It's a multinational, multicultural bar that doesn't care about race, gender identity, or anything else.

listings.name: Goen
listings.content: Goen in Hyehwa is a Japanese restaurant that offers a variety of dishes, including sushi, sashimi, and other traditional Japanese cuisine. The restaurant is known for its fresh ingredients and authentic flavors, providing a comfortable dining experience in a casual setting.

listings.name: Beonteu Seoul
listings.content: Located between Cheonggyecheon and Jongno, it is a three-story large bakery cafe that features a large space and a variety of bakery menus. In particular, it offers a leisurely atmosphere where people can share coffee and bread while enjoying the view of Cheonggyecheon.

listings.name: Artist Bakery
listings.content: It is a bakery specializing in various kinds of salt bread, featuring a savory and salty taste.

listings.name: Coffee one
listings.content: Located in Gwanghwamun, it is famous for its fat sandwiches and various puddings.

listings.name: SioPangya Gwanghwamun D Tower Branch
listings.content: Based on authentic Japanese salt bread recipes, it is a takeout specialty store that provides rich salt bread using French gome butter.

listings.name: Sseolgeuregori Stroop waffle
listings.content: This cafe specializes in Stroop waffle, an authentic Dutch dessert, and serves fresh waffles that are made on the fly.

listings.name: Hotel Bricks
listings.content: It's a quiet hotel. It provides free luggage storage and free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Bong House
listings.content: Laid-back friendly guesthouse with Internet, Wi-Fi, purifier, washing machine, air-con, refrigerator, cable TV, gas oven, microwave oven, hair dryer, iron with ironing board and dryer for a fee of ₩5,000. The Bong bar which is right next to the Bong house. With each night stay you can claim 1 free beer from the bar.

listings.name: Hostel Korea
listings.content: Friendly English/Chinese-speaking staff. Free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free laundry, air-con, hot water.

listings.name: Seoul Guest House
listings.content: Basic rooms with air-con in a traditional Korean-style house. Shared bathrooms, free Wi-Fi, and TV. For a higher price you can purchase a room with a private bath, television and computer with Internet. Some find it spartan, other like its homey feel, friendly owner and big, fluffy guard dog.

listings.name: Wind Road & Flower Guesthouse
listings.content: Free internet, laundry also available (but not free). The friendly staff speaks good English.

listings.name: Yim's House
listings.content: This excellent value hotel is unsure whether it caters to businessmen or backpackers. Rooms are clean and spacious, and Mr. Yim speaks fluent English.

listings.name: Golden Pond Guesthouse
listings.content: Comfortable, young atmosphere, with decent bathrooms and a friendly owner and staff. Two computers available for free Internet use, Wi-Fi throughout. This place is near a lot of pubs and restaurants, but very quiet when you sleep. No curfew. All staff is ready to hang out with guests every night. Sometimes they serve Korean meals for free. Kitchen, free laundry.

listings.name: Hotel Artrium Jongno
listings.content: There are free Wi-Fi and breakfast services. English and Japanese are available.

listings.name: Cheonggye Stream
listings.content: This stream has been restored to a verdant tourist attraction after long being covered by a busy freeway. You can walk many kilometers along its path through the very center of Seoul. Be cautious during the rainy day, because it may be flooded.

listings.name: Deoksugung
listings.content: Deoksu Palace vividly contrasts with the other nearby palaces like Changdeok Palace. Built during the mid-15th century, the architecture of the buildings inside are heavily influenced by Western designs. Hence, you will see a fusion of Korean and Western architecture. The stone-wall narrow way around the palace is a beautiful and famous path for the lovers, although there was a myth that they would break up when they visit, because the Family court, which people go to get divorced, was located near here. You can go now since it moved to Seocho-gu.
listings.price: Adults (19 to 64 years old): ₩1,000 (groups: ₩800), children (aged 7–18) and soldiers: ₩500 (groups: ₩400), children 6 and under, seniors 65 and over: free

listings.name: Namdaemun Gate
listings.content: The Great South Gate is an iconic symbol of Seoul and has been designated as National Treasure Number 1. Particularly beautiful when floodlit at night, and best combined with a visit to the adjacent Namdaemun Market. Much of the structure was destroyed by arson in 2008, although a faithful reconstruction was completed in 2013. Formally known as 'Sungnyemun' (숭례문, 崇禮門). The other city gates can be found in the neighboring Jongno district.

listings.name: Myeong-Dong Cathedral
listings.content: Designed by a Coste priest, and build with financial support from the Paris Church Department, this was the house of Bum-Woo Kim and purchased by Marie Jean Gustave Blanc (under the Korean name Gamilro Kim). With a successful trade agreement in 1887, the cathedral was finally built in 1898. This building was the first church built with bricks. The height of the building proper is 23 m, but with the addition of the spires, the full height is 45 m. Bricks used in the building were made in Korea and come in about 20 different shapes, as well as colors ranging from greyish color to dark wineish color. The cathedral was a place where many democratic events took place in the 1970s and 80s, especially in the June Democracy movement in 1987.

listings.name: T.um
listings.content: The future of technology can often be seen today in South Korea, and SK Telecom have created a museum dedicated to it! Exhibits change frequently due to the rapid pace of technology being shown. Preschoolers not allowed. Online pre-registration necessary, make sure to reserve early as its gets full weeks in advance.

listings.name: Seoul Museum of Art
listings.content: Renovated from an old court building, it mainly exhibits contemporary art works. You can see installments and video arts as well as paintings and sculptures. A cafe is with a souvenir shop on the first floor.

listings.name: Seoul City Hall
listings.content: The old city hall was built under Japanese rule and it was renovated to a public library. In back of the old hall, the huge new city hall was built. In the basement, there is Citizen Hall, where musical performances and exhibitions are held for citizens. City Hall Square, in front of the hall, is open to public and political demonstrations. Every winter, Ice rink opens at the Square.

listings.name: Culture Station Seoul 284
listings.content: A culture center at the old Seoul Station. It was built in 1925 during the Japanese Colonial period, and the center of the Korean railway until 2004 when the current building for KTX opened. It reopened in 2011 as a culture center, and it hosts many exhibitions. The pre-modern architecture inspired by the Lucerene station (which has burnt down) offers unique sight among the glassy buildings of Seoul.

listings.name: Seoullo 7017
listings.content: A former motorway turned into pedestrian walkway. Opened in 2017, it offers a unique view above the cars and rails, with gardens and cafes along the path. Night view with car lights and neon signs is especially beautiful.

listings.name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
listings.content: A central cathedral of the Diocese of Seoul. It was first built in 1920s and has a blended architecture of neo romanesque style with Korean traditional components.

listings.name: Bank of Korea Money Museum
listings.content: You can find out about 20,000 rare domestic and foreign currencies held by the Bank of Korea and the money manufacturing process and the country's economic process.

listings.name: Korea Financial History Museum
listings.content: It is a space where you can see Korea's financial development.

listings.name: Stamp Museum
listings.content: It is a space where you can see the process of mail change and various stamps of the world.

listings.name: Rice Museum
listings.content: It is a space where you can learn about the history of rice.

listings.name: Agricultural Museum
listings.content: It is a space where you can see various exhibitions on agriculture and traditional agricultural culture.

listings.name: Seoul Animation Center
listings.content: Seoul Animation Center (48, Sogong-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea) is a space where you can read over 30,000 comic books and animations for free, and is comprised of a 1st and 1.5-story duplex. Except for Mondays and other designated closed days, ‘Comics Cafe’ on the first floor is open from 10:00 to 20:00, and the admission fee is free. ‘Ani Picnic’ on the 2nd floor is open from 10:00 to 18:00, and the admission fee is 4,000 won for adults and 6,000 won for children. You can meet popular Korean characters such as Pororo and Tayo in person.

listings.name: Seven Luck Casino
listings.content: The casino is only accessible to foreigners (it is illegal for Korean citizens to gamble), so remember to bring your passport. Various card tables and slots are available to play. There is a bar and cafe that serve food and drinks, although expensive.

listings.name: Sparex 24
listings.content: This jjimjilbang or Korean sauna occupies two levels of mall basements. B3 is the entrance, big luggage store near reception, valuables storage at reception, shoes locker, separate showers and bath for men and women (with another larger locker, shared key with shoes locker, missing ventilation so if got wet clothes because of rain, let them out else won’t dry; bar soap) and an extra sleeping room per gender. B4 is the jjimjilbang itself (Korean village replica, saunas, common and "individual" sleeping spaces - individual can accommodate 2 persons), food court. aircon, Wi-Fi (not necessarily in all corners), power plugs (mostly side table and few common areas), water fountains hot/cold. Staff has limited English and not very friendly but lot of explanations on wall in Korean, English and Japanese. Unless taking the special ticket, you can't get out and come back without paying again. Outside food and drink not allowed (except water). After paying at reception, get clothes and key, take shower, after bath/saunas and enjoy. few big TVs in common areas. small basic pillows available. no blanket provided. Likely busier on weekends and lot of people staying night until after 8am on Saturdays.
listings.price: Day arrival (5:00-20:00) ₩ 12,000 (child 7000), night arrival ₩ 15,000 (8000), out ticket ₩ 20,000. Food court meals ₩ 5000-30,000, drinks 3000-7000, snacks 2000-4000 including chips and instant noodles
listings.address: 247 Jangchungdan-ro, Jung District, Seoul, Corée du Sud

listings.name: Gogung
listings.content: Specialty restaurant for bibimbab at a moderate price.

listings.name: Jeonju Jungang Hoegwan
listings.content: This Korean restaurant specializes in the Jeonju variety of bibimbap, which features different ingredients and spices than other bibimbap dishes. Delicious and healthy.

listings.name: Samarkand
listings.content: In the heart of "Central Asian Town", which has Russian, Mongolian, Uzbek, and Central Asian restaurants. Wander around and discover the area a bit - you'll be rewarded with delicious food and an exotic experience.

listings.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
listings.content: Beef gyoza soup, unique dish but tasty.

listings.name: Nampomyeonok
listings.content: This is a restaurant specializing in cold buckwheat-based noodles (Pyongyang’s cold noodles). This is a place visited by former presidents such as Moon Jae-in, Lee Myung-bak and Yoon Seok-yeol. This restaurant is located in a lively narrow alley in an area dense with office buildings, and consists of a room with table-style seating and cushion-style tables.

listings.name: Myeongdong Korean BBQ Mongvely
listings.content: A popular all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ restaurant, offering unlimited premium pork and beef grilled over charcoal. With multilingual menus, a self-service buffet of fresh banchan, sauces, and a DIY ramen station, Mongvely combines local flavor with tourist-friendly service.

listings.name: 82Olliienjeu
listings.content: American-home-style restaurant with a cute interior.

listings.name: Daeyeop Eulijoro Branch
listings.content: Restaurant that specializes in Pyongyang naengmyeon and various Pyongyang food.

listings.name: Yeonhaejang
listings.content: It is a restaurant specializing in pork small intestine hot pot that features a clean and modern interior, and is loved by many customers even if the waiting is long. They have gopchang hot pot with a variety of side menus, and the soup of the hot pot boasts a deep and thick taste and uses fresh gopchang without any odor. In addition, it is sold as a meal kit, so you can enjoy it easily at home.

listings.name: Gangsanok
listings.content: Opened in 1958, the restaurant specializes in traditional soybean dishes that serve only soybean noodles in the summer and serve soybean meal for the rest of the year. It is open for only two and a half hours a day, and needs to be careful when visiting because it can be closed early when the ingredients are exhausted. It consists of thick and savory soybean soup and chewy noodles, and is served with kimchi.

listings.name: Bakgane Bindaetteok Main Branch
listings.content: It is the representative restaurant of Gwangjang Market, which has been around since 1966, and serves savory and crispy bindaetteok by grinding 100% green beans directly into a millstone. It is also popular with foreign tourists, has a variety of menus and friendly service.
listings.address: jongrogu jongro32 street 7 gwangjang market 1st floor

listings.name: Hanwoojeong
listings.content: Korean BBQ restaurant specializing in 1++ Korean Hanwoo beef, Korea’s highest-quality beef grade. Inspired by the elegance of a traditional hanok, Hanwoojeong provides refined Korean dining and a warm, sophisticated atmosphere. Guests can experience carefully selected cuts including sirloin, striploin, tenderloin and other premium specialties, complemented by Korean side dishes and classic accompaniments.

listings.name: RAndy's Bar
listings.content: Foreign-owned bar in front of Hankook University of Foreign Studies known for a varied clientele, great pool table, and affordable prices. Has Red Rock and Hoegaarden on tap.

listings.name: Mezz Bar
listings.content: Bar known for cocktails

listings.name: Levenbroee
listings.content: Known for beer but also due to the view from the bar, which is amazing.

listings.name: 2MOON Cafe & Pub
listings.content: Low key, cozy cafe tucked away on the rooftop of a low building. Serves tea, coffee, drinks and cocktails. Quiet and very atmospheric at night, great for conversations, popular with and seemingly known only to locals. Owner speaks fluent English, studied in Texas and is happy to chat. Some of the clothing made downstairs by indie designers is sold here too.

listings.name: Jaehaeseok
listings.content: It is a pudding specialty cafe that boasts a unique vintage interior and cozy atomosphere.

listings.name: Asoto Bakery
listings.content: It is a bakery with a cute atmosphere where you can feel the Japanese Kitsaten sensibility.

listings.name: Gonggangap
listings.content: It is a dessert cafe located in Euljiro, especially famous for pudding bingsu and various cakes

listings.name: Ling Ling
listings.content: It is a space famous for its Y2K sensibility and kitschy interior. It offers a variety of desserts and drinks, and cakes and jelly sodas are especially popular. The interior of the store is cozy and has many photo zones, making it a great place to take pictures. Also, cute props and goods are on sale, so it entertains visitors.

listings.name: Bekarong Bagel
listings.content: A handmade bagel specialty store, all bagels are hand-rolled and feature a light, chewy texture. A takeout specialty store, it also offers a variety of cream cheese and bagel sandwiches, and it's affordable and cost-effective.

listings.name: Able Hostel/Guesthouse
listings.content: New, comfortable, young clientele, with decent baths and a friendly owner and staff. Each room has computers available for free Internet use, Wi-Fi throughout. This place is near Dongdaemun Market but very quiet when you sleep. No curfew. Kitchen, free laundry.
listings.address: No. 205, Unit 1, Kumho twin tower, 89-1, Gwanghui-dong

listings.name: IMI Hotel
listings.content: At the higher end of the love hotel spectrum, some rooms feature Japanese spas and oxygen generators.

listings.name: Namsan Guesthouse
listings.content: In the shadow of Seoul Tower in Namsan Park. Free Internet access, free breakfast, kitchen.

listings.name: Seoul Backpackers
listings.content: Backpacker hangout with English-speaking staff. Free Internet. Laundry ₩5,000.

listings.name: Silloam Sauna
listings.content: This is a very large jjimjilbang with great facilities, but the family atmosphere of other jjimjilbangs is sometimes lacking. The locker-room staff will stow oversized luggage if you ask, and a morning wake-up call can be arranged. Sleeping facilities are excellent, clean, comfortable and usually fairly quiet. There are two large dormitories for men and women, plus a snorers' room which sounds like a dragon's lair. The dormitories are arranged unconventionally into lines of bunk beds, more like an open capsule hotel than a standard sleeping floor. In the communal area there are various hot rooms, an ice room, a large gym, a PC room, singing and games rooms and a restaurant. The sauna area has 6 main pools with supposedly healthy minerals and showers. Includes access to public baths, exercise facilities, and various entertainment rooms.

listings.name: Zaza Backpackers
listings.content: Helpful English speaking staff help you to feel right at home. Free Wi-Fi, 24 hr access, Private bathroom in each room. 24 hr security, towels and hairdryer for hire, parking. Tour info and booking service. Free international phone.

listings.name: Seoul Municipal Youth Hostel
listings.content: Once the epicentre of terror and torture of the Korean Central Intelligence Agency before democracy, its headquarters is now a government-run youth hostel that provides affordable accommodation. Young travellers under 24 are entitled to a discounted price. Outside the hostel there is also a basement used as a torture chamber, which is refurbished as a museum.

listings.name: Ibis Hotel Myeongdong
listings.content: Very central, free internet access.

listings.name: Lotte Hotel
listings.content: Grand old lady of downtown Seoul's hotels with 1,300 rooms, all kept in tip-top shape. The obvious choice for ornate Korean luxury.

listings.name: Plaza Hotel
listings.content: Completely redesigned as Korea’s luxury boutique hotel in 2010, The Plaza is now an exceptionally beautiful, independent luxury hotel in the heart of the business, shopping, and entertainment districts of Seoul.

listings.name: Shilla Seoul
listings.content: One of the city's premier hotels. It was built by the Park Chung-hee government in 1967 as the state guest house for visiting foreign dignitaries, and was converted to a luxury hotel in 1979. While the hotel guest rooms are in a modern 1970s high-rise building, the original state guest house, known as Yeong Bin Gwan and built in a traditional Korean architectural style, has been preserved on the hotel property and can today be rented for events such as weddings and conferences. It is a popular venue for South Korean celebrities and tycoons to get married.

listings.name: Se-Jong
listings.content: This hotel has the beautiful view including the Namsan Tower

listings.name: Olympic Park
listings.content: Built for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Seoul Olympics. A lake, a large field covered with the grass, and a square with sculptures are very popular among visitors. It is frequently visited by brides and grooms to take their wedding pictures. There are a couple of courses that are ideal for jogging or walking. In addition, the outdoor stage and the six stadiums are often used for concerts and other special events. Also a well known modern art museum named SOMA Museum is in the park. It features modern artworks by both Korean and international artists.

listings.name: Iljasan Park
listings.content: Park with sports facilities, many herb gardens and an astronomical observatory.

listings.name: Seokchon Lake
listings.content: Actually two lakes divided by a road, surrounded by park with several playgrounds. This park is something of an oasis in the middle of the skyscraper landscape. There is also a bar inside Seokchon Lake, so you can enjoy beer with the lake in the background.

listings.name: Lotte World Tower
listings.content: Enjoy the view from the fifth tallest building in the world. Be sure to check the weather before entry. The Lotte World Tower is a 555.7-metre (1,823 ft), 123-story skyscraper located in Sincheon-dong, Songpa District. It opened to the public in 2017, and is the tallest building in South Korea and the sixth tallest in the world.

listings.name: Seoulchakbogo
listings.content: It is also a place where used books are collected and various cultural performances are held. There is also a cafe. It also has huge amounts of used books donated and sold and operated by the Seoul Metropolitan Government. If you like books, this place is recommended.

listings.name: Songlidan load
listings.content: A hot place for young people these days. There are so many delicious restaurants and pretty cafes here. There are also many hidden cafes all over the place.

listings.name: Lotte World Aquarium
listings.content: The Lotte World Aquarium, which created the closest environment to nature for "Another Sea" sea friends who recreated the marine ecosystem of the five oceans around the world, is harmonized with ocean friends from all over the world. You can experience the aquarium directly and learn the importance of the sea while feeling it.
listings.address: 300 Lotte World Mall B1 to the Olympic Games

listings.name: 291 photographs
listings.content: This place is inside Lotte Tower Mall and various photos of photographers are hung. There are 500 pictures and you can buy the pictures you want.

listings.name: Seoul Baekje Museum.
listings.content: Seoul Baekje Museum (Korean: 한성백제박물관) is a museum in South Korea. Based on the natural silhouette of the nearby Mongchontoseong, the appearance of Seoul Baekje Museum was shaped a ship of Baekje in honor of Baekje. Seoul Baekje Museum is a civic lifelong education center with an emphasis on the educational role. There are a variety of Baekje artifacts and vividly embodied materials on ancient history of the Korean peninsula.

listings.name: Songpa Book Museum
listings.content: Songpa Book Museum is the first public book museum in the country. The design of the building was created with the motif of the layers of a bookshelf. The first floor consists of a reading space, a book experience exhibition room, and a cafe. The second floor consists of a digital content experience space, a creative space, and an outdoor space for reading. Lectures or educational programs are also held in the open studio on the first basement floor.

listings.name: SOMA Museum of Art
listings.content: SOMA Museum of Art opened in 2004, and has become Songpa's representative art museum. It exhibits various paintings and outdoor sculptures, and regularly hosts special exhibitions on various themes.

listings.name: Jamsil Sports Complex
listings.content: This large sports complex centered around Jamsil Olympic Stadium, built in 1976 and host to most of the competitions in the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Though its heady Olympic heydays are long past, this sports complex is still very much active and frequently hosts various cultural and sporting events, most frequently concerts and baseball games. At Jamsil Baseball Stadium, Doosan Bears and LG Twins are home to this arena. Baseball here is very popular. It is, in fact, probably the most popular team sport in the entire country. You can feel the craze during the match. Booking tickets is tricky for non-Korean speakers. It's probably best to book tickets through an agency or third party instead of directly online. You can buy tickets offline at the stadium, but weekend games(Friday, Saturday, Sunday) are usually sold out. This place will begin construction this year as the last.

listings.name: Lotte World
listings.content: This complex has a Lotte Department Store, a theatre which hosts the show Ballerina Who Loves a B-Boy, a Lotte luxury hotel, a large indoor ice skating rick, and a traditional Korean folk museum. However, what it is most famous for is one of the world's largest indoor theme park. Lots of rides. Atlantis rides, especially outdoors, are enough to make you have fun.Though it may seem attractive on a rainy day, others will have the same idea. Especially on the weekends and on holidays, if it's raining, watch out for mind-numbing lines.
listings.price: All-day passes: ₩62,000 for adults, ₩54,000 youth; after 16:00 passes: ₩50,000 for adults, ₩43,000 for youth. For more detailed pricing information, please click here

listings.name: Lotte World Ice Rink
listings.content: The ice rink is located on the first floor of Lotte World. Even if you don't use Lotte World rides, you can use it separately. It's a great way to feel the atmosphere of Lotte World in a short time and at a reasonable price. There are many good restaurants around here, so you can enjoy delicious food after enjoying the ice rink. Resurfacing times: daily 12:50-13:10, 14:00-14:30, 16:00-16:30, 17:30-18:00, and 20:00-20:30.

listings.name: Viking Sweep
listings.content: This is a buffet of unlimited food, especially lobster. It is expensive.

listings.name: Ashley Queens
listings.content: This is the highest Ashley Queens in the class. It has the most kinds of food and makes various foods such as Japanese, Korean, and Korean food. The price is not expensive, so you can eat it with satisfaction.

listings.name: Yorihanennamja
listings.content: Inside, you can enjoy a pleasant atmosphere, and nice food.

listings.name: Godosik
listings.content: It is not a typical meat restaurant but a house that sells pork like a steak. It tastes great.

listings.name: Olderplate
listings.content: The venue does not use ground or ground meat for more than 2 days, and prides itself for using fresh ingredients inside a clean environment.

listings.name: DanDi
listings.content: This house specializes in Daechang rice, which can only be found in Korea.

listings.name: Lalabread
listings.content: It is a store that sells sandwiches etc. by baking bread by itself. You can enjoy brunch or lunch lightly.

listings.name: Outback Steak House
listings.content: It is about a 10-minute walk from exit 2 of Jamsil Station on line 2 and 8. It is about a 10-minute walk from exit 1 of Seokchon Station on line 8.

listings.name: 9 con me
listings.content: Parking is available in front of the store. Songpa Women's Cultural Center near the full train. Or on-road parking lots along the road or paid parking lots nearby.

listings.name: Songridan's taste
listings.content: It is a fusion restaurant in Songridan-gil. The neat wooden interior is impressive.

listings.name: never sleeps pizza
listings.content: You must use the nearby public parking lot for the parking lot. Search the Songpa Neighborhood Park parking lot on the navigation (29, Songpa-daero 42, Songpa-gu, Seoul). It's an eight-minute walk from Pizza Neverslip.

listings.name: goteat
listings.content: - Parking available: Dosan Park branch, Ilsan branch, Uijeongbu Minrak branch, Dongtan branch. No parking: Songridan-gil Branch, Olympic Park Branch, Seongsu Holy Water Branch, Yeonnam Branch, Anguk Branch, Bojeong Cafe Street Branch, Yongsan Branch, Gangnam Gadnonhyeon Branch. Reservations are only available at Dosan Park.

listings.name: London Bagel Museum
listings.content: One of the most famous bagel shops in Korea. You can make a non-face-to-face reservation through the CatchTable app. It is recommended to make a reservation and then visit the mall.

listings.name: Gordon Ramseyburger
listings.content: The first Gordon Ramsay burger in Asia. Enjoy a high-end concept burger restaurant from world-renowned 3 Michelin-starred chef Gordon Ramsay.
listings.address: B1F, Lotte World Mall, 300 Olympic-ro, Songpa-gu

listings.name: Chunghwaog
listings.content: This restaurant serves kukbap, a national dish of Korea. It's one of the most delicious restaurants in Korea. You can control the spiciness with the red seasoning called dadaegi.

listings.name: Bangeog
listings.content: This is the place to go for Korean-style barbecue. Along with the meat, you can also enjoy "so-mac," a mixture of Korean soju and beer.

listings.name: obut restaurant
listings.content: A cozy Western-style bistro in Wirye New Town with a warm, inviting atmosphere. It is local favorite for its succulent steaks and flavorful pasta dishes, offering a perfect setting for a relaxed meal.
listings.address: Room 203, 2nd floor of the shopping mall, 120, Wirye Plaza-ro, Songpa-gu

listings.name: jejugan
listings.content: A Jeju-inspired BBQ spot specializing in premium aged pork belly. The staff grills the meat at your table, allowing for a perfectly cooked, hassle-free dining experience.

listings.name: Sincheon
listings.content: A large nightlife district. This is not Sinchon (신촌), another nightlife district that is frequently mixed up because of the name - Sinchon is in Seodaemun/Mapo, which is the opposite side of the city and mainly caters to university students. Sincheon, on the other hand, is populated more by local businessmen; in Korea, getting drunk together with co-workers is seen as essential to building working relationships, which is one of the reasons why Korea has such a high rate of drinking. If you are a foreigner working in a Korean office or visiting Korea for a business trip, you may find yourself visiting this neighbourhood.

listings.name: Onhwa (온화)
listings.content: The cafe is in Songni-Dan-gil and the souffle pancake is a famous cafe. Inside, it gives a beige color.

listings.name: JenJen
listings.content: It specializes in cake and milk tea. Store has a good reputation

listings.name: Take a shower (테이크 어 샤워)
listings.content: This place has a cute charm and is a great cafe to post photos on SNS.

listings.name: Anggwa
listings.content: This is the first Dorayaki house in Korea. Dorayaki is an unfamiliar dessert and will be curious. The price is low, too.

listings.name: Onjung (온정)
listings.content: This is a famous house for raw fruit tart.

listings.name: pepper
listings.content: It's located on the second floor of the cafe complex and Gyeongyang katsu building.You can go around the building and come up the stairs to the entrance.

listings.name: Blue Bottle Jamsil Cafe
listings.address: 300 Blue Bottle Jamsil Cafe in Olympic-ro

listings.name: pit a cake
listings.content: It is a handmade cake restaurant that uses fresh fruit and milk cream.

listings.name: Antique Coffee Jamsil Branch
listings.content: Parking is prohibited in the store, so the nearest parking lot is Yuseong parking lot (paid).
listings.address: Jamsil branch of Antique Coffee on the 1st floor of 21-16 Baekje Gobun-ro 41-gil, Songpa-gu

listings.name: Craft island (크래프트아일랜드)
listings.content: It is a beer house and is also well prepared for beer.

listings.name: Jamsil branch of 1987 loop tower (1987루프탑라운지)
listings.content: This bar is characterized by its roof top. You can eat while watching the night view of Seoul.

listings.name: Motoqurasi (모토쿠라시)
listings.content: Izakayada. They mainly sell sake, a Japanese liquor.You can also eat seafood-related foods.

listings.name: Radiohead pub (라디오헤드 펍)
listings.content: You can taste five draft beer managed by a winner of the Philsten Bartender contest, and you can enjoy a selection of wines and hard work for ₩3,000-100,000. You can request songs. We try to play them according to the latest pop, old pop, rock, hard rock, and blues.

listings.name: Tong (통)
listings.content: Salmon sashimi and alcohol can be eaten in a quiet atmosphere.

listings.name: Lotte hotel world (롯데월드호텔)
listings.content: It is a five-star hotel with perfect facilities around it and the station is also near.The price is a little expensive.

listings.name: Dellight hotel (딜라이트호텔)
listings.content: It's a reasonable price for a night's sleep. There is Seokchon Lake nearby.

listings.name: Hotel Lake
listings.content: Hotel Lake is 11 minutes' walk from Seokchon Station Exit 8 of Subway Line 8. Seokchon Lake, a downtown rest stop, is across from the hotel, and Lotte World Tower, the 6th highest place in the world, is 15 minutes away on foot.

listings.name: Sofitel Ambassador Seoul Hotel & Serviced Residences
Hotel Infini
listings.content: Free private parking and a business center are available, as well as a 24-hour front desk.

listings.name: Jamsil Tomgi Hotel
listings.content: Rooms are fitted with a flat-screen TV and tea and coffee-making facilities. Both air conditioning and heating are provided. Private bathrooms come with a hairdryer. Laundry and ironing can be done in the hotel. Luggage storage is provided at the front desk. The hotel also offers fax and photocopying services.

listings.name: Sofitel Ambassador Seoul Hotel & Serviced Residences
listings.content: The hotel will provide guests with air-conditioned rooms with a closet, a coffee machine, a fridge, a safety deposit box, a flat-screen TV and a private bathroom with a bidet. The rooms are equipped with an electric tea pot, while some rooms also feature a kitchenette with a microwave and a minibar. At Sofitel Ambassador Seoul Hotel & Serviced Residences, rooms have a seating area. Breakfast is available every morning, and includes buffet, continental and Italian options. Guests can use the business center or relax in the bar.

listings.name: Signiel Seoul
listings.content: All rooms are carpeted and fitted with a mini-bar, fridge, coffee machine, safety deposit box and flat-screen TV. Private bathroom includes a hairdryer, free toiletries, slippers and toilet with an electronic bidet. Staff at Signiel Seoul can assist guests with luggage storage, valet parking and concierge services. Dry cleaning, laundry, trouser press and ironing services are available at a surcharge.

listings.name: Hotel the Castle Banyi
listings.content: The rooms in the hotel are equipped with an electric tea pot. Featuring a private bathroom with a bidet. At the accommodation rooms include air conditioning and a flat-screen TV.

listings.name: Seodaemun Prison
listings.content: The prison was built in 1908, and became infamous during the Japanese occupation when it was used to torture, starve and execute Korean political prisoners. Actual prison cells, wax figures and videos are used to demonstrate the shocking brutality experienced there. Most signs are in Korean although volunteer guides can describe the sights in English. The content may not be suitable for those of a sensitive nature.

listings.name: World Cup Stadium
listings.content: It was South Korea's main stadium in the 2002 World Cup and is home to FC Seoul.

listings.name: Seodaemun Museum of Natural History
listings.content: At this museum you can learn more about geology, archeology and biology. Plenty of fossils on display, interactive exhibitions and various activities for kids.

listings.name: Worldcup Park
listings.content: Worldcup Park has several sections. Sky Park is the most popular for the Silver Grass Festival. The park used to be a waste landfill.

listings.name: Trickeye Museum
listings.content: Trickeye Museum features optical illusion paintings and installations. Divided into six themed galleries, visitors can freely touch, step inside 3D exhibits and take photos.

listings.name: Castle Praha
listings.content: A Czech brewery and restaurant, with outside facade being a replica of Prague's Astronomical clock.

listings.name: Korean Film Museum
listings.content: The Korean Film Museum is divided into a permanent exhibition and temporary exhibitions. The permanent exhibition introduces the history of Korean films in chronological order and operates an experience zone. The exhibitions are held under various themes so that you can watch and enjoy Korean movies from a new perspective.
listings.address: 400 World Cup Buk-ro, Mapo-gu, 1st floor of the Korea Film Archive

listings.name: The Hyundai Seoul
listings.content: A Hyundai Department Store brand, it's home to all things fashion, hip-hop, food, and dessert.

listings.name: Nanji Hangang Park
listings.content: Nanji Hangang Park is one of South Korea's famous Han River parks, known for its water features, fountains, festivals, and camping.

listings.name: Mang-Won Hangang Park
listings.content: Seoul's first Hamsang Theme Park, Hangang Park is famous for its water-based leisure activities.

listings.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
listings.content: Yeouido Hangang Park is famous for being the site of the World Fireworks Festival, held every October.

listings.name: Hongdae Playground
listings.content: The area around here in Hongik University is completely packed with shops and restaurants aimed solely at University students. Definitely an interesting way to spend some hours exploring the streets and see how Korean students let their hair down. Dinner can be had in this area at student prices, or avail yourself to one of the many street stalls serving Korean student street food.

listings.name: Hongjecheon Stream
listings.content: Hongjecheon Stream is an urban stream in Seoul, South Korea, flowing through the districts of Seodaemun-gu and Mapo-gu. It provides a recreational space for residents with walking paths, greenery, and scenic views along its banks.

listings.name: Jamdubong the 9
listings.content: Korean pork belly with river views. It is located on a dock floating on the river.

listings.name: Sosinitsso (소신이쏘)
listings.content: This fusion galbi restaurant serves spicy Korean short ribs with cheese.

listings.name: DamSan (담산)
listings.content: This is the place to go for loin ribs, Korean gondre namulbap, and kimchi jeon.

listings.name: GoSamE (고삼이)
listings.content: This local restaurant serves Korean-style grilled fish and stir-fried squid.

listings.name: GonangZi (고냉지)
listings.content: The restaurant's signature dishes are bibimbap and kimchi stew.

listings.name: HanLimDonGa (한림돈가)
listings.content: This is the place to go for samgyeopsal, a Korean-style barbecue.

listings.name: Miga
listings.price: ₩ 8000-45000, Jeyuk Ssambap ₩20,000 for 2 or more persons (₩12,000 if single person), Osam Bulgogi ₩26,000 for 2 or more (₩15,000 if alone)

listings.name: okmyeonga
listings.content: chicken-specialized small restaurant with different types of noodles.

listings.name: Grain Seoul
listings.content: Build-your-own brunches and all-day mains in a thoughtful open space. English spoken.

listings.name: Shin Migyeong Hongdae Dakgalbi
listings.content: Great dakgalbi place just off the main night market street. Simple menu, cook it at your table. Good value and big portions!

listings.name: jinjin
listings.content: Jinjin is a Chinese restaurant in Seoul's Mapo-gu, offering a focused menu of about 10 dishes, known for its quality and traditional flavors. It has received the Michelin Bib Gourmand award for its good value. Signature dishes include Menbosha (shrimp toast) and stir-fried crab with egg white.

listings.name: spaccanapoli
listings.content: Known for authentic Neapolitan-style wood-fired pizza, this restaurant is highly praised for its use of traditional methods, including a real wood-fired oven. Popular menu items include the Margherita and Gorgonzola pizzas, and the ambiance is often described as vibrant and lively.

listings.name: Uwa
listings.content: Located in the bustling Hongdae area, Uwa offers a modern dining experience with a focus on casual yet trendy dishes. It is often visited for its eclectic menu and relaxed atmosphere, making it a go-to spot for younger crowds and students.

listings.name: Hongdae SsiBooOng
listings.content: A cozy café known for its desserts and drinks, this spot is famous for its photogenic ambiance. It’s a popular location for both locals and tourists looking for a quiet spot to relax in the busy Hongdae district.

listings.name: yakitorimook
listings.content: The restaurant handles fresh native chicken every day, grills it with the finest splints, and serves customers immediately

listings.name: Analog Garden
listings.content: Brunch menu has just one item: omelette-on-toast, but can be customized with add-ons. Rather popular with foreigners, service can be a bit chaotic but food is worth it. About 17000₩ for brunch with coffee.

listings.name: Nambuk Tongil
listings.content: A long-running Korean restaurant specializing in North Korean-style mandu. Popular dishes include mandu hot pot, dumpling soup, chicken kalguksu and mung bean pancakes.

listings.name: lodge 190
listings.content: Lodge 190 is a cozy café located along the Hongjecheon Stream in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul. Known for its signature French toast made with baguette and topped with seasonal fruits, the café offers a relaxing ambiance with views of Hongjecheon. The menu includes a variety of desserts, such as matcha shaved ice and yogurt bowls. Lodge 190 is also pet-friendly.

listings.name: Beer O'Clock
listings.content: This Canadian-run bar serves great pizzas and other grub in addition to showing sports on the big screen and offering darts. Weekends are pretty wild at this joint.

listings.name: Woodstock
listings.content: Around since 1991, the bar has prompted a slew of copycats but is the best place to hear classic rock and pop. The sound system is awesome and the owner/DJ knows his stuff. Expect large crowds Friday and Saturday nights and seeing people dance next to their tables. Great place to mix with Koreans of all ages.

listings.name: Piehole
listings.content: Piehole is a dessert café located in Sinchon, Seoul, specializing in a variety of homemade sweet pies and tarts. The interior features a cozy and vintage atmosphere with distinct, home-style decorative touches throughout the seating areas. It operates daily in the Sinchon commercial district, serving as a well-known local spot for dessert and coffee.

listings.name: Miroir
listings.content: Psychedelic hippie hangout with psytrance F and Sa, 1960s and 70s rock during the week.

listings.name: 17°C
listings.content: Located in Hongdae, chocolate bingsu and dark chocolate drinks are especially popular, making it an attractive space to serve a variety of chocolate drinks and desserts. The inside of the store is cozy and neat.

listings.name: Before Blooming
listings.content: It is a cake specialty cafe that offers a variety of cakes using seasonal fruits. Especially, fig cakes are popular, and the store provides a cozy and clean atmosphere to communicate with. It features a convenient ordering system through a kiosk and friendly service. In addition, it is known as a place for special days with the availability of holecakes.

listings.name: Cafe Gongmyeong Yeonnam Branch
listings.content: It is a large cafe that offers top-class coffee and fresh baked bakery with cozy interior design. This is a space where customers can enjoy a variety of desserts, with ample seats and cozy lighting to help them relax. In particular, the signature drink 'Rise Latte' and the signature dessert 'Biscuit Shoe' are receiving positive reviews from many visitors. Also, various books are available throughout the cafe.
listings.address: mapogu yeonhuiro 11 Korea Patent and Technology Promotion Agency Building 1st floor

listings.name: Sweet Hz
listings.content: This cafe offers a variety of matcha and hojicha drinks and desserts with its cute interior and Japanese sensibility. In particular, matcha basque cheesecake and whipped cream cake are popular, and the dessert is not sweet and features the original taste of the ingredients. The interior of the cafe is decorated with warm lights and cute props, providing a comfortable atmosphere.

listings.name: Mandongjegwa
listings.content: Located in Yeonnam-dong, this takeaway specialty store offers a wide variety of bread. The interior of the store is compact, neat, and full of savory bread. The staff kindly provides tasting bread to help customers choose. Specifically, garlic baguette is a signature menu, featuring a rich garlic sauce and a soft texture. There is a wide variety of menus, and reservations are also available for convenience.

listings.name: Orangji
listings.content: It is a cafe famous for its cute interior design and cute desserts. Serving various matcha drinks and desserts, heart pancakes and kitty matcha tiramisu are especially popular. The inside of the cafe is white-toned and cozy, with props everywhere, making it a great place to take pictures. It is a place to enjoy dessert with friendly service.

listings.name: Joaendoseun
listings.content: It is a cafe famous for French toast and milk tea. It is decorated with a cozy and emotional interior, and customers appreciate the moist texture and unique taste of French toast. In particular, the combination of Maldon salt and maple syrup is impressive as French toast has a crispy outside and soft inside.

listings.name: Peullemmeu
listings.content: Located in Yeonnam-dong, the cafe offers a variety of desserts, such as souffle pancakes and croffles. This cafe has a cozy and quiet atmosphere, and it has various amenities for customers to spend their time comfortably. Souffles are cooked on the spot and take about 20-30 minutes. Specifically, souffle pancakes feature a soft and fluffy texture.

listings.name: Turn down service
listings.content: It's a quiet Woody emotional cafe, where LP music plays. Inside, it's compact and spacious, and offers a variety of handmade tarts and coffee menus. Specifically, the signature menu, Kernel Latte, boasts a savory and sweet taste with homemade nut creams on it. There is a two-hour limit.

Located in Yeonnam-dong, the cafe offers a variety of desserts according to the four seasons and boasts a cozy and warm atmosphere. It is decorated with an emotional interior, and the menu changes from season to season, and desserts using figs and corn are especially popular. Beverages and desserts are being evaluated for their excellent visuals and taste.

listings.name: Maybe Cake
listings.content: It is famous for whipped cream cakes that use fresh strawberries, and it is operated by reservation, so advance reservations are required. The cake is made with 100 percent animal whipped cream, which boasts a moderately sweet taste without being greasy. Also, the interior is decorated with a cute and pretty atmosphere.

listings.name: Think Fruit
listings.content: It is a cafe that specializes in souffles and various fruit desserts in Hongdae. The inside is neatly decorated in white tone, and it boasts a bright atmosphere with full glass. Souffles are made right on order and of high quality using Hagen-Dazs ice cream. It is especially popular with customers as it offers a wide variety of menus using seasonal fruits.

listings.name: Rahel's kitchen Hongik Univ. Branch
listings.content: It is a cafe that offers soft souffles and a variety of brunch menus. Inside, it is decorated with cute white and pink-toned interiors, and it is a space that feels open through the window. There are many kinds of souffles, and they are handmade and have a fresh taste. In addition, they can be accompanied by pets and come with chairs for infants.

listings.name: Cafe Jang Ssam
listings.content: Located in Hongik University, this cozy dessert cafe serves a wide variety of dacquoise and cakes. Specifically, dacquoise is loved by many visitors for its fluffy texture and the combination of chewy cream, and the price is also reasonable. The interior is decorated with warm wood-tone interiors.

listings.name: Kitchen 205
listings.content: It is a place that provides desserts produced and sold on the same day using fresh strawberries throughout the four seasons. Strawberry cakes here are especially loved for their freshness and quality. The store has a clean and cozy atmosphere.

listings.name: Thrive Hongik Univ. Branch
listings.content: It is a cafe famous for its unique interior design and various souffle menus that contain Jeju's sensibility. In particular, souffle is loved by many visitors for its soft and fluffy texture, and it is an attractive space to enjoy with various drinks.

listings.name: Just Danbi
listings.content: It's a real-time live place to deliver freshly baked crepes as soon as you order.

listings.name: Judimari Hongik Univ. Branch
listings.content: It is a dessert cafe famous for its cute interior and various pudding menus. In particular, the soft texture and rich taste of the pudding are loved by many visitors. The interior of the store is decorated with cute props, making it a great place to take pictures.

listings.name: Cafe Letter
listings.content: It is a bakery cafe that boasts a warm sensibility and cozy atmosphere, offering various kinds of bakery and specialty coffee. Especially, strawberry vanilla bun and croissant sandwiches are recommended as signature menus, and the cozy interior and meticulous service provide a comfortable experience for visitors.

listings.name: Pioni Hongik Univ. Branch
listings.content: A cake specialty store that has been in operation since 2008, it is famous for its fresh strawberry cream cake made using 100 percent animal whipped cream and fresh strawberries. The interior of the store is cozy and clean, and it is a popular destination for many customers as it offers a variety of drinks and cakes. In particular, cakes that are carefully made with all ingredients boast reliable and edible quality.

listings.name: Kokorokara
listings.content: A dessert shop in Yeonnam-dong specializing in handmade desserts and baked goods.

listings.name: Pig Company Hongdae Korean BBQ
listings.content: Pig Company is a pork-focused Korean BBQ spot in Myeongdong, known for cauldron lid grilling and crispy Korean fried chicken made fresh in-house. Built for sharing at the table.

listings.name: Bangrang Hostel
listings.content: 1 min from subway station, 2 min from airport bus stop.

listings.name: Hongdae Guesthouse
listings.content: Clean, spacious rooms with high ceilings, ondol heating, aircon, hot water. English spoken.

listings.name: Seoul Walker Guesthouse
listings.content: The owner, Mr. Yoo, speaks Korean, Japanese, and English. He is very friendly and always asks where you will go (in the morning) and where you went (at night). Laundry service is available for ₩5,000/cycle, which he will operate. He offers taxi service to and from Gimpo and Incheon airports, for ₩30,000 and ₩60,000, respectively. He has many pamphlets in different languages, books, a computer and printer, and WiFi. KakaoTalk and KakaoStory are available for communication. No curfew, but keep silence after 23:00. There is a code lock for security.

listings.name: The Win Boutique Hotel
listings.content: The basement dorm has a large common area and several bathrooms. Everything is clean, and access is 24-hr. Staff presence is minimal; reservations are recommended.

listings.name: Best Western Premier Seoul Garden Hotel
listings.content: Formerly the Holiday Inn, located in the Mapo area across from Yeouido Island.

listings.name: Chocolate Tree
listings.content: 109-91 Nogosan-dong, Mapo-gu (4 min from Line 2 Sinchon stn exit 7). Friendly and adorable English- and Chinese-speaking staff, free breakfast (toast, jam, peanut butter, eggs, coffee and tea), free wifi, free international phone call, free laundry, dryer, A/C, hot water, rooftop terrace, common area with kitchen. All rooms are equipped with desktop computer, refrigerator, big flat TV with cable TV on the wall. you can get some chocolates at the reception at anytime. private from ₩50,000/night with own bathroom.

listings.name: Bonghwasan
listings.content: A 160-m-high mountain from where there are good views over the city. The mountain together with the surrounding park is a popular place for short hikes. Also worth seeing is the Sasingak Shrine at the southern side of the mountain.

listings.name: Seoul Forest
listings.content: Seoul's own Central Park, at the northern bank of Han. It's composed of five smaller parks, the culture & art park, the natural ecology forest, the natural hands-on experience learning garden, the ecological wetland garden and the Han river waterfront park as well as an outdoor stage and a big playground.

listings.name: Geonguk University Museum
listings.content: A museum with Korean historical artifacts. The main attraction here is the Donggukjeongun, a set of six books from the 15th century describing how Chinese characters should be pronounced. These were the first such teaching books in Korea.

listings.name: King Sejong Memorial Hall
listings.content: Memorial hall dedicated to the culturally most important king in Korean history.

listings.name: Ilgam-ho
